Lesson 3: Comparative Advantage and Trade
Section: Countries work the same way

Countries work the same way
The textbook's example: Brazil can grow a lot of sugar cane per acre but not much wheat; the U.S. is the reverse. Brazil has the comparative advantage in sugar cane, the U.S. in wheat. On a graph, Brazil's PPF is steeper.
note: Show this with a graph as an example. Additionally, look through the artifact. When it mentions a graph and it would be relevant to include a graph, include one.
